epithet.en: The wandering sailor who narrates the voyage of the Pequod
epithet.da: Den vandrende sømand der fortæller om Pequods rejse

1.modern-en: Ishmael introduces himself — a restless man who goes to sea whenever the world grows too heavy on land — and announces his intention to ship on a whaling voyage.

2.modern-en: Ishmael arrives in New Bedford on a cold December Saturday and searches for lodging, ending up at the Spouter-Inn.

7.modern-en: Ishmael visits the Whaleman's Chapel and meditates on the marble tablets to dead sailors; he confronts his own mortality before sailing.

10.modern-en: Ishmael and Queequeg spend a Sunday in cozy friendship at the inn; Ishmael reflects that a good-natured cannibal can be a better man than a bad-natured Christian.

16.modern-en: Ishmael goes alone to choose a ship for their voyage; guided by Queequeg's idol Yojo, he signs on to the Pequod.

17.modern-en: Ishmael waits outside Queequeg's door during his day-long Ramadan fast, growing increasingly worried before Queequeg emerges peacefully.

41.modern-en: Ishmael reflects that he too shouted with the crew when Ahab revealed the quest for the White Whale — swept up in a wild, mystical sympathy he could not explain.

42.modern-en: Ishmael meditates on the whiteness of the whale and why it terrifies him beyond rational explanation — whiteness as the color of dread itself.

102.modern-en: Ishmael recalls measuring a whale skeleton in the Arsacides; he had the dimensions tattooed on his arm to preserve them.

136.modern-en: The epilogue: Ishmael alone survives the Pequod's destruction, saved by Queequeg's coffin-buoy; the Rachel picks him up, 'another orphan.'

epithet.en: The obsessed captain who drives the Pequod's crew toward the White Whale
epithet.da: Den besatte kaptajn der driver Pequods mandskab mod den hvide hval

16.modern-en: Ahab is mentioned ominously before he is seen: the owners Peleg and Bildad describe him as a man changed since losing his leg to the White Whale.

18.modern-en: Ahab is referenced as the captain Pip and the crew wait to meet.

19.modern-en: Elijah hints darkly at what Ahab and the crew have signed on for, unsettling Ishmael and Queequeg.

20.modern-en: The crew busies itself with final preparations; Ahab has not yet appeared on deck.

21.modern-en: As the ship departs, a figure that may be Ahab is glimpsed briefly in the shadows.

22.modern-en: Ahab still does not appear on deck as the Pequod sails into the Atlantic winter.

27.modern-en: Ahab finally shows himself on deck, his scar-seamed face and ivory leg planted in the gimbal, surveying his crew.

28.modern-en: Ahab paces the deck day and night, his ivory leg thumping; the crew observes him but keeps its distance.

29.modern-en: Stubb politely suggests Ahab cover his window; Ahab erupts in fury and humiliates him — revealing a nature that will brook no challenge.

30.modern-en: Ahab alone on deck smoking his pipe; he throws the pipe overboard, finding it no longer gives comfort.

34.modern-en: Ahab presides over the silent, hierarchical dinner at the cabin table — a ceremony of control and distance.

36.modern-en: Ahab summons the crew to the quarterdeck and nails a gold doubloon to the mast; he announces the quest for the White Whale and wins the crew to his purpose with rum.

37.modern-en: Ahab alone at sunset, soliloquizing: he knows his purpose is fixed and beyond reason, driven by something larger than will.

38.modern-en: Starbuck's soliloquy reveals his dread: Ahab's madness has overpowered all reason on the ship.

39.modern-en: Stubb muses on Ahab's effect on the crew — deciding the only sensible response is to laugh and follow.

41.modern-en: Ahab's obsession with Moby Dick is explained: the whale bit off his leg, and Ahab transferred all the world's evil onto the creature.

44.modern-en: Ahab studies his charts late at night, plotting the whale's likely seasonal routes with frightening precision.

46.modern-en: Ahab entertains surmises about his crew's obedience; he privately knows profit for owners motivates men, and uses that to his advantage.

48.modern-en: Ahab reveals his secret boat crew — five shadowy men led by Fedallah — who appear to lower for whales; the crew is shocked.

50.modern-en: Ahab's private boat and Fedallah are now known to the crew; speculation and unease grow.

51.modern-en: A silvery jet appears at night on the horizon, luring the ship onward; Ahab is rapt, believing it may be Moby Dick.

73.modern-en: Ahab orders the head of a sperm whale kept alongside; he will use it as a mirror for his own thoughts.

99.modern-en: Ahab gazes at the gold doubloon nailed to the mast; he reads in it a reflection of himself — the obsessive who sees everything as a sign.

100.modern-en: Ahab hails the Samuel Enderby and interrogates its captain about Moby Dick; he sees the captain's lost arm as a badge of kinship, but the man's pragmatic peace enrages him.

106.modern-en: Ahab's ivory leg is cracked in a stumble; he orders the carpenter to make a new one, irritable and impatient.

108.modern-en: Ahab supervises the making of his new ivory leg and harangues the carpenter in a dark, philosophical monologue.

109.modern-en: Starbuck discovers the oil barrels are leaking and urges Ahab to heave to for repairs; Ahab refuses at first but finally yields — a rare moment of practicality.

113.modern-en: Ahab has Perth the blacksmith forge a special harpoon for Moby Dick, baptizing it with the crew's blood rather than water.

118.modern-en: Ahab destroys his sextant in rage, declaring he will navigate by the stars alone in a defiance of science.

119.modern-en: During the typhoon, the corpusants glow on the mast-tips; Ahab seizes the chains and delivers his defiant speech, refusing to be frightened by fire or nature.

120.modern-en: Ahab and Starbuck have a tense late-night exchange; Starbuck nearly despairs of the ship's fate.

123.modern-en: Starbuck stands over the sleeping Ahab with a musket, tormented by the chance to end the voyage; he cannot pull the trigger.

124.modern-en: Ahab declares the ship's compass wrong and fashions a new needle himself — a demonstration of will over instrument.

125.modern-en: Ahab dismisses the log and line and trusts himself alone to know the ship's position.

127.modern-en: Ahab orders the coffin converted into a life-buoy; he and the carpenter have a grim philosophical exchange over death.

128.modern-en: Ahab refuses to help the Rachel search for her missing captain's son — the White Whale is all that matters.

129.modern-en: Ahab sends the clinging Pip away with a warning that his own madness could infect the boy.

130.modern-en: Ahab sits at the masthead, watching; a hawk steals his hat and the omen darkens the crew's mood.

131.modern-en: Ahab passes the Delight, whose captain lost men to Moby Dick; Ahab brushes off the warning and sails on.

132.modern-en: Ahab and Starbuck share a rare, tender moment — Ahab weeps briefly and wonders what drives him — before hardening again.

133.modern-en: Moby Dick is sighted; Ahab is first to spot the whale and descends from the masthead to lead the chase on the first day.

134.modern-en: The second day of the chase: Ahab's boat is capsized, his ivory leg snapped; he refuses to give up and orders a new boat.

135.modern-en: The third day: the White Whale destroys the boats, rams the Pequod, and sinks her; Ahab is tangled in the harpoon line and dragged into the sea.

epithet.en: Ishmael's tattooed harpooner companion from the South Sea island of Rokovoko
epithet.da: Ishmaels tatoverede harpuner-ledsager fra sydhavsøen Rokovoko

3.modern-en: Ishmael is forced to share a bed with the strange, tattooed harpooner Queequeg at the Spouter-Inn; initial terror turns to uneasy coexistence.

4.modern-en: Ishmael wakes with Queequeg's arm around him; they share breakfast in comfortable silence; Queequeg's essential gentleness becomes apparent.

5.modern-en: Queequeg quietly eats his steak at breakfast; his manner among the other sailors is dignified and untroubled.

6.modern-en: Queequeg walks through New Bedford with Ishmael; passersby stare but he remains serenely indifferent.

7.modern-en: Queequeg visits the chapel but leaves before the benediction; death holds no particular dread for him.

10.modern-en: Queequeg and Ishmael spend Sunday together; Queequeg shares his tobacco, and they swear a friendship pact.

11.modern-en: Queequeg and Ishmael lie in bed talking and dozing; the intimacy of their friendship is settled.

12.modern-en: Queequeg's backstory is given: a prince from Rokovoko who stowed away on a whaling ship to see the Christian world, and became a harpooner.

13.modern-en: Queequeg and Ishmael travel by ferry and Queequeg rescues a man who mocked him from drowning — a demonstration of his moral instincts.

15.modern-en: Queequeg and Ishmael arrive in Nantucket and settle at the Try Pots inn.

16.modern-en: Queequeg sends Ishmael alone to choose the ship; his idol Yojo has told him this is the right way.

17.modern-en: Queequeg spends the day in a Ramadan fast, sitting motionless on the floor; Ishmael panics but Queequeg emerges unharmed and content.

18.modern-en: Peleg questions Queequeg's fitness as a cannibal; Queequeg demonstrates his harpooning skill and is immediately signed on.

22.modern-en: Queequeg is one of the first to go aboard the Pequod as she sails; his place among the crew is established.

27.modern-en: Queequeg is named as one of the Pequod's three harpooners, assigned to Starbuck's boat.

28.modern-en: Queequeg is part of the crew adapting to shipboard life under Ahab's remote command.

36.modern-en: Queequeg raises his harpoon with the rest when Ahab rallies the crew to the quest for Moby Dick.

40.modern-en: Queequeg participates in the midnight forecastle scene, dancing and joining in the sailors' songs.

47.modern-en: Queequeg and Ishmael weave a mat together; Ishmael reflects on fate, free will, and chance in the rhythm of their weaving.

48.modern-en: Queequeg is in the whaleboat during the first lowering; the boat is swamped but Queequeg saves the day with calm skill.

54.modern-en: Queequeg is featured in the Town-Ho's Story as a capable harpooner whose reputation precedes him.

61.modern-en: Queequeg kills a whale during Stubb's successful hunt; he calmly inserts a cutting spade between the flurries.

74.modern-en: Queequeg's tattoos are compared to the carved surface of the sperm whale's head — mysterious hieroglyphs of meaning.

78.modern-en: Queequeg falls into the sperm whale's case while baling it; Tashtego hauls him out, and the episode becomes darkly comic.

87.modern-en: Queequeg is in the boats during the Grand Armada chase, one of the harpooners who works among the circling whales.

91.modern-en: Queequeg is part of the crew during the encounter with the French ship Rose-Bud.

94.modern-en: Queequeg joins the sailors in squeezing the spermaceti; the scene is one of communal warmth and peace.

110.modern-en: Queequeg falls gravely ill and asks the carpenter to make him a coffin; he recovers but keeps the coffin, converting it to a sea-chest.

114.modern-en: Queequeg is among the crew during the pleasant Japanese cruising ground scenes.

119.modern-en: During the typhoon, Queequeg is among the crew handling the ship in the storm.

122.modern-en: Queequeg works aloft in the storm, lashing the yard as lightning plays around them.

126.modern-en: Queequeg's coffin is converted into the ship's life-buoy after the original is lost.

127.modern-en: Queequeg's coffin-buoy sits on deck; Ahab and the carpenter discuss it in dark philosophical terms.

130.modern-en: Queequeg is part of the watching crew as the Pequod nears the ground where Moby Dick is expected.

133.modern-en: Queequeg is in the boats on the first day of the chase after Moby Dick.

134.modern-en: Queequeg rows in the second day's chase and survives the whale's destruction of the boats.

135.modern-en: Queequeg is presumably lost with the Pequod on the third day; his coffin becomes Ishmael's life-buoy.

epithet.en: The Pequod's first mate, a brave Quaker sailor and the voice of reason against Ahab
epithet.da: Pequods førstestyrmann, en modig kvæker-sømand og fornuftens stemme mod Ahab

21.modern-en: Starbuck is briefly seen directing loading operations as the ship departs.

22.modern-en: Starbuck takes command of the ship's watch in Ahab's absence; he is the responsible, competent officer the crew relies on.

26.modern-en: Starbuck is introduced: a lean Nantucket Quaker, brave but not recklessly so, who believes courage without cause is wasted and life is sacred.

27.modern-en: Starbuck is established as first mate; Queequeg is his assigned harpooner.

34.modern-en: Starbuck sits first and most rigidly at Ahab's cabin table — the hierarchy of the ship is physical.

36.modern-en: Starbuck alone objects to Ahab's quest, arguing the owners hired them for oil, not revenge; Ahab overwhelms him with passionate will.

37.modern-en: Starbuck's internal soliloquy: his sanity is overpowered; he is helpless against Ahab's madness yet cannot fully surrender to it.

38.modern-en: Starbuck soliloquizes at dusk: he is a sane man among madmen, unable to stop what is coming.

39.modern-en: Stubb reflects on Starbuck's powerlessness against Ahab.

41.modern-en: Starbuck did not shout with the crew at the quest's announcement; his dissent is noted.

48.modern-en: Starbuck commands one of the whaleboats on the first lowering; the storm catches them and they nearly perish.

61.modern-en: Starbuck oversees the whale kill; he is the professional officer ensuring the hunt goes correctly.

100.modern-en: Starbuck watches as Ahab's interaction with the Samuel Enderby's captain confirms how far Ahab has gone.

109.modern-en: Starbuck discovers the oil barrels are leaking and reports it to Ahab; Ahab's initial fury gives way — a rare concession.

119.modern-en: During the typhoon, Starbuck notices the three anchors sway loose; he fears the ship is being driven onto a lee shore.

120.modern-en: Starbuck urges Ahab to turn home; Ahab refuses; Starbuck's despair deepens.

123.modern-en: Starbuck stands over the sleeping Ahab with a loaded musket and considers ending the voyage — the novel's most agonizing moral crisis; he cannot do it.

124.modern-en: Starbuck watches Ahab construct a new compass; he is appalled but helpless.

132.modern-en: Starbuck and Ahab share an unexpectedly human moment on deck; Ahab weeps, and Starbuck believes briefly that he might turn back — but Ahab hardens.

133.modern-en: Starbuck pleads with Ahab not to hunt on the first day of the chase; Ahab ignores him.

134.modern-en: Starbuck warns Ahab after the second day's losses; his pleas grow more desperate.

135.modern-en: Starbuck cries out that the voyage is impious and doomed; Ahab drives on and Starbuck goes down with the ship.

epithet.en: The Pequod's easy-going second mate, who faces danger with a laugh and a pipe
epithet.da: Pequods afslappede andenstyrmann, der møder faren med et grin og en pibe

22.modern-en: Stubb receives a nightcap from the charitable Charity as the ship departs — the first sign of his good-humored relationship with the world.

26.modern-en: Stubb is introduced as second mate: a Cape Cod man, happy-go-lucky, who smokes his pipe in the calmest of emergencies.

27.modern-en: Stubb is confirmed as second mate with Tashtego as his harpooner.

29.modern-en: Ahab furiously humiliates Stubb when Stubb politely asks him to muffle his ivory leg on deck at night; Stubb retreats, bewildered.

30.modern-en: Stubb watches Ahab throw his pipe overboard and shakes his head.

31.modern-en: Stubb tells Flask about his dream: Ahab kicked him with his ivory leg, and a merman told him it was an honor.

34.modern-en: Stubb sits second at the cabin table, behind Starbuck; the hierarchy is strictly enforced.

36.modern-en: Stubb joins the rest of the crew in the oath to hunt the White Whale.

39.modern-en: Stubb muses alone that laughter is the only sensible response to working for a madman like Ahab.

41.modern-en: Stubb is among the crew drawn into Ahab's obsession.

48.modern-en: Stubb commands a whaleboat on the first lowering; he is methodical and cool in the chase.

50.modern-en: Stubb comments sardonically on the revelation of Ahab's secret boat crew.

61.modern-en: Stubb successfully kills a large sperm whale; he directs the kill from his boat with calm authority.

64.modern-en: Stubb eats his whale steak at midnight by lantern light, ordering the cook to prepare it rare; it is a scene of strange, comic self-satisfaction.

73.modern-en: Stubb and Flask kill a right whale on Fedallah's mysterious advice; Stubb jokes throughout but is quietly unnerved.

91.modern-en: Stubb boards the French ship and tricks the crew into leaving an ambergris-laden whale; he gets the prize through wit.

94.modern-en: Stubb oversees the squeezing of the spermaceti; the crew falls into a dreamy camaraderie around the tubs.

115.modern-en: Stubb encounters the jolly Bachelor and joins in the merriment briefly.

116.modern-en: Stubb kills another whale; the dying whale turns its head toward the sun — a moment of strange dignity.

117.modern-en: Stubb keeps watch over a killed whale through the night, repelling sharks.

119.modern-en: Stubb tries to keep spirits up during the typhoon as the crew is frightened.

121.modern-en: Stubb and Flask lash the anchors securely in the storm and discuss Ahab's madness.

133.modern-en: Stubb is in the boats on the first day's chase; he is splashed by Moby Dick's flukes.

134.modern-en: Stubb survives the second day's boat smashings and is rescued.

135.modern-en: Stubb calls out 'I grin at thee, thou grinning whale!' as the Pequod sinks; he goes down with a laugh.

epithet.en: The Pequod's third mate, short, pugnacious, and without philosophical doubt
epithet.da: Pequods tredjestyrmann, lille, stridbar og uden filosofisk tvivl

22.modern-en: Flask receives a ginger-jar from Charity as the ship departs.

27.modern-en: Flask is introduced as third mate: a pugnacious, short Vineyarder who thinks whales are his personal adversaries and kills them without reflection.

31.modern-en: Flask hears Stubb recount his Ahab dream; he is unimpressed.

34.modern-en: Flask sits last at the cabin table and must eat rapidly before the next rank takes the plates.

36.modern-en: Flask joins the Moby Dick oath along with the rest.

41.modern-en: Flask is mentioned as part of the crew caught up in Ahab's will.

43.modern-en: Flask hears a strange sound from below and discusses it with another sailor — the hidden crew.

48.modern-en: Flask commands a whaleboat in the first lowering; he is practical and without sentimentality.

49.modern-en: Flask and Ishmael bob in a swamped boat after the first lowering; Flask is philosophically unmoved.

50.modern-en: Flask is the first to raise the question of Fedallah's presence aboard.

61.modern-en: Flask participates in the whale hunt; Daggoo is his harpooner.

64.modern-en: Flask watches Stubb eat his midnight whale steak and is bemused.

73.modern-en: Flask and Stubb together kill a right whale at Fedallah's urging.

78.modern-en: Flask oversees the dangerous baling of the case.

121.modern-en: Flask and Stubb lash the anchors in the storm and grimly discuss the ship's fate.

133.modern-en: Flask is in the boats on the first day of the final chase.

134.modern-en: Flask survives the second day's wreckage.

135.modern-en: Flask is lost when the Pequod sinks on the third day.

epithet.en: The small Black cabin boy from Alabama who loses his mind in the open sea
epithet.da: Den lille sorte kahytsdræng fra Alabama der mister forstanden på det åbne hav

27.modern-en: Pip is mentioned as the Pequod's small Black cabin boy; the narrator notes he never returned from the voyage.

40.modern-en: Pip is heard being ordered to strike the bell; he takes part in the wild forecastle scene, playing his tambourine.

93.modern-en: Pip is called on to substitute in a whaleboat; when he jumps overboard in fright, the boat cannot stop for him; floating alone in the vast sea, his mind breaks — he has seen God's foot on the treadle of the loom.

99.modern-en: Pip watches as each man interprets the doubloon in his own way; he offers his own broken riddle — all that remains of his shattered reason.

110.modern-en: Pip wanders the ship in his madness, muttering prophecies; he is treated gently by Queequeg, whose coffin now dominates the deck.

125.modern-en: Pip trails Ahab and grasps his hand; Ahab tells him to stay by him and be the ship's true log — the one honest mind left.

127.modern-en: Pip sits on the coffin and delivers a mad oration; he is sad and strange, the ship's broken jester.

129.modern-en: Ahab sends Pip away from him, fearing that the boy's genuine innocence will weaken his resolve.

epithet.en: The mysterious Parsee prophet secretly brought aboard by Ahab as harpooner and oracle
epithet.da: Den mystiske parsiske profet Ahab hemmeligt tog med om bord som harpuner og orakel

48.modern-en: Fedallah appears for the first time when Ahab's secret boat crew emerges; he is tall, turbaned, and sinister.

50.modern-en: The crew speculates about Fedallah's origins; Stub wonders if he is the devil himself.

51.modern-en: Fedallah is seen at the mast-head, watching; his presence adds an uncanny atmosphere.

73.modern-en: Fedallah whispers to Ahab that capturing a right whale alongside a sperm whale is an omen of luck; Ahab orders it done.

99.modern-en: Fedallah gazes at the doubloon; he reads its signs with an inscrutable expression.

100.modern-en: Fedallah stands silently in the background as Ahab meets the Samuel Enderby's captain.

130.modern-en: Fedallah watches from the mast-head as the Pequod closes in on Moby Dick's grounds.

132.modern-en: Fedallah and Ahab exchange a glance during the symphony — the Parsee's prophecies weigh on the captain.

133.modern-en: On the first day of the chase, Fedallah rows in Ahab's boat; he is seen standing erect as they close on Moby Dick.

134.modern-en: Fedallah is lost on the second day of the chase — dragged down by the whale-line coiled around Moby Dick.

epithet.en: The retired harpooner-turned-preacher who delivers the sermon on Jonah before the voyage
epithet.da: Den pensionerede harpuner-omvendte præst der holder prædiken om Jonas inden rejsen

8.modern-en: Father Mapple enters the Whaleman's Chapel; his commanding, weather-beaten presence fills the room.

9.modern-en: Father Mapple delivers his sermon on Jonah: the story of disobedience, the whale's belly, and the redemption found only in total surrender to God's will.

18.modern-en: Father Mapple is remembered by Ishmael as having baptized Queequeg or confirmed his fitness in the eyes of heaven — the moral counterweight to Peleg's pragmatism.

epithet.en: The enigmatic prophet on the dock who warns Ishmael and Queequeg about Ahab
epithet.da: Den gådefulde profet på kajen der advarer Ishmael og Queequeg om Ahab

19.modern-en: Elijah approaches Ishmael and Queequeg after they sign on the Pequod; he asks unsettling questions about what they know of Ahab, hinting at dark things ahead.

21.modern-en: Elijah is seen again near the ship at dawn, watching as the men go aboard; he may have glimpsed shadowy figures — Fedallah's crew — slipping onto the ship.

28.modern-en: Elijah's prophecy comes to mind as Ahab finally appears on deck — the sense of fated doom he planted is now flowering.

48.modern-en: Elijah's vague warning about Ahab's secret crew is retrospectively confirmed when Fedallah and his men emerge.

64.modern-en: Ishmael recalls Elijah's warnings as the voyage takes its darker turn.

epithet.en: The retired captain and part-owner of the Pequod who signs on the crew
epithet.da: Den pensionerede kaptajn og medejer af Pequod der ansætter mandskabet

16.modern-en: Peleg signs Ishmael on the Pequod; he is gruff and nautically experienced, warning that Ahab is a great captain but unusual.

18.modern-en: Peleg is initially hostile to Queequeg's signing on as a cannibal; Queequeg's demonstrated skill with a harpoon wins him over.

19.modern-en: Peleg dismisses Elijah's dark hints about Ahab as nonsense, though uneasiness shows under his bluster.

20.modern-en: Peleg oversees the final loading and preparation of the Pequod.

22.modern-en: Peleg and Bildad take the Pequod out of harbor by tugboat; Peleg shouts nautical orders with gusto and nostalgia.

106.modern-en: Peleg is remembered as one of the owners whose approval Ahab needed and got; his authority over the ship has passed.

epithet.en: The pious, penny-pinching Quaker co-owner of the Pequod
epithet.da: Den fromme, pengeknibnende kvæker-medejer af Pequod

16.modern-en: Bildad is present as Ishmael signs on; he offers an absurdly low lay and reads scripture to avoid discussing money.

18.modern-en: Bildad initially refuses Queequeg on religious grounds but accepts him once Peleg vouches for his value as a harpooner.

20.modern-en: Bildad oversees the stowing of provisions, fussing over costs.

22.modern-en: Bildad and Peleg pilot the Pequod out; Bildad's last act is to throw food and hymns to the crew; he weeps as the ship departs.

epithet.en: A Gay Head Native American harpooner, Stubb's man and among the Pequod's finest hunters
epithet.da: En Gay Head-indiansk harpuner, Stubbs mand og en af Pequods fineste jægere

27.modern-en: Tashtego is introduced as the second harpooner: a Gay Head Native American with the unmistakable bearing of a born hunter.

28.modern-en: Tashtego is among the crew that first sees Ahab emerge on deck.

34.modern-en: Tashtego eats at the second table after the mates — the harpooneers' station.

36.modern-en: Tashtego crosses his harpoon with the other harpooneers in Ahab's oath ceremony.

47.modern-en: Tashtego is at the masthead when the word comes down of possible whale sightings.

48.modern-en: Tashtego is in Stubb's boat during the first lowering.

54.modern-en: Tashtego is mentioned among the harpooners in the Town-Ho's Story.

61.modern-en: Tashtego throws the first harpoon in Stubb's whale kill.

74.modern-en: Tashtego is at the masthead and sights the whale.

78.modern-en: Tashtego falls into the sperm whale's case while baling it; Queequeg dives in and pulls him out feet-first, like a baby being born.

87.modern-en: Tashtego participates in the Grand Armada chase.

122.modern-en: Tashtego is in the mast, lashing yards in the typhoon, muttering against the thunder.

130.modern-en: Tashtego keeps watch from the masthead as the ship approaches Moby Dick's hunting ground.

133.modern-en: Tashtego is at the masthead on the first day of the chase and among the first to see Moby Dick.

134.modern-en: Tashtego is in the boats on the second day.

135.modern-en: Tashtego hammers a sky hawk to the mast as the Pequod sinks — the last visible act aboard the ship before it disappears.

epithet.en: A giant African harpooner from a coastal village, Flask's man aboard the Pequod
epithet.da: En kæmpestor afrikansk harpuner fra en kystby, Flasks mand om bord på Pequod

27.modern-en: Daggoo is introduced as the third harpooner: an enormous, golden-earringed African whose physical presence is magnificent.

34.modern-en: Daggoo eats with the other harpooneers at the second table.

36.modern-en: Daggoo crosses his harpoon in Ahab's ceremony.

40.modern-en: Daggoo participates in the midnight forecastle scene.

48.modern-en: Daggoo is in Flask's boat during the first lowering.

59.modern-en: Daggoo is at the masthead and cries out at the sight of a giant squid — mistaken momentarily for the White Whale.

61.modern-en: Daggoo takes part in Stubb's whale hunt.

64.modern-en: Daggoo assists in the cutting-in of Stubb's whale.

74.modern-en: Daggoo is mentioned among the harpooneers as Ishmael examines the sperm whale's head.

78.modern-en: Daggoo is near Tashtego during the dangerous case-baling operation.

87.modern-en: Daggoo is in the boats during the Grand Armada chase among the school of whales.

133.modern-en: Daggoo rows in the chase on the first day.

134.modern-en: Daggoo is in the boats on the second day of the chase.

135.modern-en: Daggoo goes down with the Pequod.

epithet.en: A fanatical Shaker prophet aboard another ship who claims Moby Dick is the Shaker God and must not be hunted
epithet.da: En fanatisk Shaker-profet om bord på et andet skib der hævder at Moby Dick er Shaker-guden og ikke må jages

1.modern-en: Gabriel is named in the opening catalogue of sailors who have gone to sea.

71.modern-en: The Pequod meets the Jeroboam; Gabriel, its mad prophet, shouts across the water that Moby Dick is divine and must not be hunted; he has paralyzed the ship's captain with religious terror.
